unavailable_fields.communication: Not applicable per observations.json capability field ('single-device task'); request.json sets distributed_backend null with a single device '0', and the completed torch trace shows no NCCL kernels, so nccl_tuning and collective_calibration have no subject.
unavailable_fields.nccl_algorithm_protocol_channels: Kernel entry names alone do not identify NCCL algorithm/protocol, and no collective executes in this single-device inference invocation, so the nccl_tuning warmed worker would have nothing to record.
unavailable_fields.per_collective_pcie_nvlink_bytes: Single-device task with host-to-device staging outside the measured invocation; device_telemetry exposes only device-wide NVML rates/utilization/memory at native sampling windows, and PCIe/NVLink traffic must not be invented from logical payload or memcpy sizes.
unavailable_fields.per_operator_peak_allocated_bytes: No remaining collector supplies tensor- or operator-level allocation attribution; the already-completed torch run's evidence (coverage.json) records association counts only (103/103 kernels associated below project, 0 unassociated, 0 ambiguous forward sequences).
unavailable_fields.cuda_max_memory_reserved_bytes: The harness samples only torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() per repeat (resnet_inference.py:43-48) and no selected collector reports allocator reserved/segment statistics.
unavailable_fields.cudnn_conv_workspace_bytes: No name in available-collectors.json exposes per-kernel workspace (ncu is present in tools but is not an available collector), and cudnn.benchmark=False selects workspaces internally.
unavailable_fields.first_numerical_divergence_site: candidate_diagnostics records only exceptions and False returns and neither compares intermediate tensors nor locates the first numerical divergence; no other available collector supplies per-site numerical error.
unavailable_fields.binding_overhead_baseline: binding_cost is not applicable before any candidate exists; observations.json contains only the baseline capability, so there is no additive candidate parent/passthrough pair to compare (it would also run in subsequent candidate resource feedback once an additive candidate exists).
unavailable_fields.clean_host_dispatch_share: python_runtime's warmed cProfile inclusive/self times are perturbed and are explicitly not clean performance scores or GPU compute durations; the evaluator already samples clean invocation latency and images_per_second via torch.cuda.synchronize + perf_counter_ns, so no clean host/GPU split is obtainable from the remaining collectors.

rationale: The frozen objective minimizes peak_allocated_bytes of one offline batch-32 FP32 ResNet-18 forward (single infer() invocation, torch.inference_mode) on one CUDA device, with a 0.95x images_per_second floor. The torch collector already ran and fully resolved the trace: 103/103 CUDA kernels associated below project, 0 unassociated, 0 root-only, 0 ambiguous forward sequences and 0 autograd ranges (inference-only), so no overlap, graph-tracing or attribution question remains that would justify selecting optional nsys. Communication-oriented collectors are excluded on evidence: the capability marks communication not_applicable ('single-device task'), distributed_backend is null, devices are ['0'] and the trace contains no NCCL kernels, making nccl_tuning and collective_calibration inapplicable, while device_telemetry's device-wide NVML readings with native windows cannot attribute the torch-allocator peak of the measured invocation and PCIe staging lies outside the measured unit. candidate_diagnostics and binding_cost act on supplied candidate files, and no candidate exists yet (observations.json holds only the baseline capability), so both are not applicable at this stage. python_runtime perturbs execution and yields no clean scores relevant to a memory objective whose throughput floor is already measured directly per repeat by the evaluator, and execution_timeline would only re-derive CPU-to-CUDA associations that coverage.json shows are already complete while its clock-alignment bounds speak nothing to allocation peaks; its gradient post-accumulate callbacks are moot under inference_mode. Therefore no additional collector is selected: the evaluator-sampled objective metrics (peak_allocated_bytes, images_per_second, latency_ms) are requested as fields, and the remaining diagnostic dimensions (allocation attribution, allocator reserved bytes, conv workspace, NCCL decisions, per-collective traffic, first divergence site, pre-candidate binding overhead, clean host/GPU split) are recorded as unavailable with observed reasons rather than approximated.
